summary: Fixed both defects the decider sent back; the product code is untouched. O-028: fitness rule 'Cancel attempts never run on the thread pool or a timer' now allows only Close's own pool call, matched by its `static aborted` lambda parameter (`\bThreadPool\.(?!UnsafeQueueUserWorkItem\(static aborted\b)`). It also refuses `new Task(`/`new Task<` (`\bnew\s+Task\s*[(<]`), and its `because` names that one exempt call site. Checked in both .NET and Python regex: 0 hits on the current file, and the pool-queued-attempt and `new Task(CancelOnce).Start()` mutants are each caught. Second defect (validate's NEW finding against build-slice): CancelIsResentUntilACallThatHadNotReachedTheKernelIsInterrupted no longer relies on a fixed 200 ms sleep. The worker now waits until the guard has sent 2 cancels, plus 100 ms, before it blocks. A mutant that delays every attempt by 300 ms reproduces validate's '1 attempts, 1 delivered' on the old test (3 of 3) and passes the new one (3 of 3). A no-resend mutant is still red. Acceptance, rules, idle full suite (337 of 337, twice), a pinned-load pass (3 of 3) and a real app run all pass.

files.why: O-028. In rule 2 (settled by SL-055), the ThreadPool pattern's exemption now covers only Close's hand-off, `\bThreadPool\.(?!UnsafeQueueUserWorkItem\(static aborted\b)`. Added `\bnew\s+Task\s*[(<]`. The `because` now names the one exempt call site and why reusing that API for attempts still fails.

Validate's NEW finding against build-slice. In CancelIsResentUntilACallThatHadNotReachedTheKernelIsInterrupted, Thread.Sleep(200) is replaced by SpinUntil(CancelAttempts >= 2, 5 s) plus Sleep(100), so the cancels that should miss have certainly been sent before the wait. Added Assert.True(sentBeforeWait, ...), raised the Join from 5 s to 10 s to cover the 5 s wait, and updated the doc comment to say why.

obligations.how: Replaced the first pattern of rule 2 with `\bThreadPool\.(?!UnsafeQueueUserWorkItem\(static aborted\b)`, added `\bnew\s+Task\s*[(<]`, and rewrote `because` to name Close's `ThreadPool.UnsafeQueueUserWorkItem(static aborted => ...)` as the one exempt call site. .NET Regex and Python re, run on the patterns read back from the yaml, agree. The current SynchronousIoCancel.cs matches 0 patterns and the Close line is still allowed. The pool-queued attempt `ThreadPool.UnsafeQueueUserWorkItem(static g => g.CancelOnce(), this, preferLocal: false);` is caught by the ThreadPool pattern. `new Task(CancelOnce).Start();` and `new Task<bool>(...)` are caught by the Task pattern. ArchitectureRulesTests, RuleCopiesAgreeTests and OptInTraitTests pass 22 of 22. rules-parity says AGREE in both shells (37 settled entries). RuleCases C-001 to C-005 all hold.

deviations: Validate's NEW finding against CancelIsResentUntilACallThatHadNotReachedTheKernelIsInterrupted was fixed in the test only, as validate suggested: wait for the guard's own attempt count, not a fixed sleep. The design's case C-004 is unchanged. The test's premise (all cancels before the wait miss) was written for a canceller that called CancelSynchronousIo inline. SL-055's per-attempt thread made 'within 200 ms' untrue under load: validate measured p50 325 ms. So the test now waits for 2 sends plus 100 ms. It still fails a canceller that never resends: that mutant was red 2 of 2 with 'the wait was never interrupted'.
not_built: C-011 (delivered-cancel latency over 2 s) and C-012 (Thread.Start throwing) still have no dedicated test. The design marked both non-material, and nothing owed asks for them.
follow_ups: The decider's reason reached this stage cut off at 'The test depends on ti…', and the index's validate entry says only 'criterion not met'. The second defect could be identified only by opening validate-slice-2.json (its NEW obligation against build-slice). The engine should carry a validate-raised build obligation into 'STILL OWED' the way it carries review findings, not leave it inside a clipped reason.

Validate's remaining reds under pinned load predate this slice and are the design's open question for a person: the 250 ms Cancel() bar in CancelInterruptsACallBlockedInTheKernel and CancellationTests, and CancelAtRandomMoments' calibration when cancel classes run in parallel. Both passed 3 of 3 in this attempt's pinned pass.
